name: structured-request-logging-p1
prompt: how should I make our logs searchable so I can trace one request across services

chunks.content: we mint a correlation id at the edge gateway and propagate it through every downstream call, so a single trace can be reassembled by filtering on that one field
switched every emitter to structured JSON lines with consistent keys (level, ts, service, trace) instead of free-form text, so the aggregator can index them
logs are shipped to the central store where you can query by the propagated trace identifier and see all hops of one request in order
every failed login is recorded with the username and source IP so security can review suspicious access patterns
a redaction filter strips emails and tokens from log fields before they leave the process
the request body is validated against a schema and a 422 is returned listing every field that failed
an alert fires when any node's disk passes 85 percent so we can prune before it fills
added a dark mode toggle that remembers the choice in local storage
the reports page can now export the current filter as a CSV download
read-heavy analytics queries were moved to a read replica to take pressure off the primary
verify the Stripe webhook signature before trusting any payment event
thumbnails are generated lazily on first request and then cached at the CDN
